newsitem.title: USA: Swiss official pledges swift probe of Jewish assets.
newsitem.headline: Swiss official pledges swift probe of Jewish assets.

text.p: A Swiss government official promised on Wednesday that Switzerland would press ahead swiftly with an investigation into assets left in Swiss banks by victims of the Jewish Holocaust.
Thomas Borer, head of a task force coordinating the investigation, told a House committee, "It is our intention and expectation that we will conclude our investigation within two to three years."
Borer was testifying to the House Banking Committee as the Swiss parliament gave final approval for a study of Swiss financial dealings with Nazi Germany and the fate of Jewish assets.

Borer said that if it was found that assets belonging to Holocaust victims were still being held wrongfully in Switzerland, the Swiss government would make every effort to return them to their rightful owners. If the owners could not be traced, Switzerland would make the money available to "relevant charities," he said.
Borer said that the new Swiss law setting up the investigation would lift banking and other professional secrecy laws for five years.
He also said that a final report on Swiss agreements with former communist countries of central Europe was expected to be ready before the end of December.
